# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001
- Strategy tried: multi-class, code-heavy candidate — 3 distinct in-body guards (payment
  normalize+auto-correct, baggage recompute, cancel-flown) + narrow return enrichment + 5
  policy rules, each grounded by live-DB replay of gold/failing args. No LEDGER rows yet
  (iter 1) to cite.
- Plateau/stall signal: none yet. Deliberately diversified levers up-front rather than
  spending the iteration on one cluster, because the biggest cluster (STALL/###STOP###) has
  no safe code lever and would otherwise strand the iteration on prose alone.
- Process note: auto-memory from prior runs was the highest-value input — it named the exact
  verified code levers and the refuted ones (wide enrichment, composite+remove), letting me
  skip re-deriving them and go straight to live verification. Verifying every code edit on the
  live tau2 DB before keeping it is cheap and caught the sign/ordering details (refund sign,
  payment_history re-sync, baggage recompute reading the CURRENT cabin).
- What to try next iteration: if accepted, attack STALL with a refusal-preserving composite
  modify tool; if rejected, read the broke={} set — the code guards are individually no-op on
  correct inputs so a rejection most likely implicates a prose rule (e.g. the confirm-then-act
  rule changing a passing trajectory), which I'd drop while keeping the verified code.

## Iteration cand_0002
- Strategy tried: switch the primary lever from in-body guards (cand_0001) to a NEW
  composite WRITE tool (`change_cabin`) for the cabin-change cluster — the largest
  cross-task cluster (11/19/37 + cabin part of 17/22). Rationale: the agent repeatedly
  CORRUPTS the flights argument on a cabin-only change (duplicated/invented segments) or
  REFUSES because it can't pre-compute the amount; a tool that rebuilds segments verbatim
  and computes the amount removes both failure modes in code. Added it WITHOUT removing the
  primitives (segment-change/held-out tasks still need `update_reservation_flights`),
  trading a little selection risk for zero capability loss.
- Verification lever that paid off: the local trajectory extractor (gold action_checks +
  compact transcript) + live-DB replay of the new tool on 5 real reservations caught that
  it reproduces gold exactly and is a safe no-op on same-cabin. Cheap, high-confidence.
- What to try next iteration: if ACCEPTED, (a) a `modify_reservation` composite bundling
  cabin+passengers+baggages for the multi-change requests (17/22), and (b) a read tool for
  cheapest-cabin fare search (task 23). If REJECTED, the DB-verified tool is unlikely to be
  the cause — bisect the policy prose (most suspect: the city-match heuristic) and keep the
  tool.

<!-- cap-evolve:meta-insights-append-below -->

## Iteration cand_0003
- Strategy tried: turn cand_0002's rejected-but-harmless lever into the "bigger effect"
  the framework asked for. cand_0002 added `change_cabin` ADDITIVELY and kept the raw
  primitives → reject 0.417, broke={} (no damage, just too weak to clear noise). This
  round I REMOVE the three update primitives (`REMOVE_TOOLS`) and expose exactly one
  mandatory composite (`modify_reservation`, all four modify dimensions) + one read tool
  (`quote_change`). No LEDGER row yet for this iter to cite.
- Plateau/stall signal: one reject since the accepted cand_0001. Lesson distilled: when a
  DB-verified tool is rejected with broke={}, the problem is almost never correctness — it
  is that the model can still route around the tool. The lever that changes behavior is
  REMOVING the escape hatch (the raw primitives), not adding another optional tool or more
  prose. "POWER/SIZE" = make the good path the ONLY path, and make it cover the whole cluster
  in one call (cabin+flights+passengers+baggage), not a slice of it.
- Verification lever that paid off again: driving the REAL adapter (`_build_candidate_tools`)
  rather than the raw module — it confirmed REMOVE_TOOLS actually filters at the get_tools
  boundary AND that the hidden primitives stay callable for delegation. Testing the raw module
  alone would have missed both (the raw module does not apply REMOVE_TOOLS).
- What to try next iteration: if ACCEPTED, freeze the modify surface and attack task 23
  (multi-booking cheapest-fare + which-certificate-absorbs-which) with a READ fare-search
  tool — the last cluster with no safe lever. If REJECTED with broke={} a third time, stop
  adding tools: bisect the policy prose (city-match heuristic is the prime suspect for
  flipping a passing trajectory) and keep the DB-verified tools.
